title: China Capitalizes on America’s Scientific Brain Drain
author: Catherine Tan
text:
Credit: Shutterstock
This summer, the departure of more than a dozen established scientists from American universities to China caused a stir in the international press. They were established figures across a variety of disciplines – mainly in the sciences – from quantum computing to biochemistry to artificial intelligence. In one high-profile example, Nobel Prize winner Omar Yaghi left the University of California, Berkeley to lead an AI research institute at Tsinghua University. Several National Academy members also left U.S. universities for positions in China. Many had spent more than a decade, and in some cases several decades, building long careers in the United States.These departures had been long in the making. Fueled by frustration with the Trump administration’s stringent immigration and national security policies in both its first and second terms, an unprecedented number of researchers say they are considering leaving the U.S.  [...]
